significance: A slender 24.5 m temple raised as the mortuary shrine of Kertanegara, the last king of Singhasari, and built to express the Shiva-Buddha synthesis he professed: a Shaivite cella holding a yoni, with Durga, Ganesha, Nandi and Brahma images, set beneath a pinnacle combining a cube with a Buddhist stupa.
story: When lightning struck the monument in 1331 the image of the Buddha Akshobhya is said to have vanished from it, a disappearance read as a manifestation of shunyata, emptiness.
